hook: Antifreeze proteins grip ice with both methyl-group dispersion and sugar hydroxyl polar contacts.
hook_turn: with both methyl-group dispersion and sugar hydroxyl polar contacts.
summary: Synthesizing antifreeze glycoprotein variants with deuterium or fluorine swaps, then testing with NMR, activity assays and simulations, supports a model that merges the older polar and hydrophobic views. Methyl groups favor contact with ice, while hydroxyls and bound water make binding selective and lasting. The evidence is consistent with the model rather than a direct view of the bound state.
title: Unifying Polar and Hydrophobic Models of Ice Recognition by Antifreeze Glycoproteins
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society
